item.title: Tesla, Xpeng Showcase Autonomous Cars in Paris
item.description: Tesla and Xpeng are competing beyond EVs and into AI, as Bloomberg's Caroline Connan explores the Cybercab and takes Xpeng's autonomous tech for a spin in Paris. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Breaking Down Big Bank Earnings
item.description: Four of Wall Street's biggest banks reported earnings on Tuesday morning. JPMorgan Chase & Co., Citigroup Inc. and Wells Fargo & Co. set a fresh record for how much they earned from lending. Herman Chan of Bloomberg Intelligence has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India-US Trade Talks Heading in Right Direction, Jaishankar Says
item.description: Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said trade negotiations with the US were close to a conclusion, though final details remained to be resolved.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: We're Back to Normal Rates, Says Ed Yardeni
item.description: Yields in the US and other advanced economies have climbed to multidecade highs, tightening financial conditions, amid higher inflation triggered by the US-Iran war and concern about budget shortfalls. Traders have responded by paring rate-hike expectations, with the amount priced into swaps across eight major economies falling by almost 200 basis points since mid-September, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Ed Yardeni, President at Yardeni Research, discusses his S&P call and why he believes rates are 'back to normal' and not 'higher for longer.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CFTC Staff Told to Retract Analysis of Suspicious Oil Trades
item.description: CFTC analysts flagged unusually well-timed trading ahead of a March 23 Truth Social post in which President Donald Trump postponed planned U.S. strikes on Iranian energy facilities. Billions of dollars in contracts changed hands in the 15 minutes before the announcement. According to sources, analysts identified traders and referred their findings to the CFTC’s enforcement division, but a senior official intervened and asked them to retract the referral. Charles Gorrivan reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bank Profits Face New Challenges
item.description: KBW Head of US Bank Research Chris McGratty joined Bloomberg Open Interest to break down what's driving bank earnings. He explains why large banks may still appeal to investors and how consumer health, interest rates and consolidation could shape what's ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Domino's Drops on Sales Growth Miss; Bumble Goes Private | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Domino's Pizza (DPZ) shares are lower after the restaurant chain reported total domestic stores comp sales growth for the third quarter that missed the average analyst estimate. - Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) shares are moving as the company reports earnings. J&J raised its profit guidance as demand for newer drugs in cancer and autoimmune diseases overshadowed more anemic growth in the company’s medical device business. - Bumble (BMBL) shares are halted on news Ithaca is taking Bumble private for $1.3 billion, with a deal price of $6.05 per share. Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd said she would “remain actively involved with Bumble” after the deal, which marks a significant change for the company that was valued at $14 billion when it went public. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: New Mountain Bets on Defensive Growth
item.description: As investors reassess private credit, New Mountain Capital’s Laura Holson says direct lending is offering attractive opportunities with wider spreads and improved lender protections. She joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why higher rates can benefit floating-rate investments, what risks borrowers face, and why her firm favors defensive-growth sectors such as industrial automation and animal health. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside the Fight Against Food Recalls
item.description: After a summer of food recalls and illness outbreaks, Neogen CEO Mike Nassif explains how testing, traceability,and data can help producers spot risks earlier and rebuild consumer confidence in a complex global food supply chain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EPA Confirms 100% Reallocation for Refinery Biofuel Exemptions
item.description: The Trump administration said it will make up for lost biofuels demand after the biggest breaks from blending mandates for refiners in nearly a decade, providing a boost for American farmers.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Elkin

item.title: Billionaire Birla Says Investment Calls Becoming Tougher Now
item.description: Billionaire Kumar Mangalam Birla said multiple global crises have made investment decisions tougher for his metals-to-retail empire that generates over a third of its business overseas.
item.dc:creator: Satviki Sanjay and Aryan Gupta

item.title: Can Infrastructure Keep Pace With AI?
item.description: Sanjiv Ahuja, Chairman & CEO, Tillman Global Holdings; Abhijit Dubey, President & CEO, NTT DATA, Inc.; Salil Parekh, CEO & Managing Director, Infosys; and Connor Teskey, CEO, Brookfield Asset Management discuss the physical constraints of scaling AI with Bloomberg's Shery Ahn at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.description: For as long as modern-day money markets have been around, there’s been one constant: Lou Crandall.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Harris

item.title: S&P 500 Record Rally Meets Risk of Peaking Earnings Growth
item.description: For Corporate America, the bar to deliver earnings growth that satisfies Wall Street’s bulls is only getting higher.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Kniazhevich

item.title: S&P 500 Slips as Chipmaker Selloff Deepens, Banks Report Results
item.description: US stocks declined on Tuesday as a selloff in chipmakers deepened and traders sorted through generally strong results from JPMorgan Chase & Co., Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and other lenders in the start to third-quarter corporate earnings season.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: LSEG in Talks to Buy Permira-Owned Credit Firm Octus
item.description: London Stock Exchange Group Plc is in talks over a potential acquisition of global credit platform Octus from private equity firm Permira, as the centuries-old stock market pushes deeper into data.
item.dc:creator: Swetha Gopinath

item.title: DGB Offers Ethan Allen CEO a Non-Board Advisory Role
item.description: DGB Investments has offered an olive branch of sorts to the head of Ethan Allen Interiors Inc. as the activist seeks to replace the furniture company’s board and chief executive officer.

item.title: Chip Selloff Rolls On as Big Bank Earnings Begin: Markets Wrap
item.description: A selloff in chipmakers deepened on concerns about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence trade, putting pressure on equity markets as Wall Street banks kicked off the earnings season.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 13
item.description: Oil held steady after three days of gains as traders booked profits from the recent rally amid persistent risks to energy supplies stretch from the Middle East to Russia.
